per_shot.note: Glowing cyan pool lands well on its rim, but the wyrm is coiled into a closed ring that reads as a bracelet or necklace, not an animal; no readable head or mouth.
Faceted pearl body with violet fin is pretty and on-palette, but the loop silhouette and blank octahedron head give no dangerous end.
Cyan halo tile bleeds nicely into the stone below, but the tiny white sprig is near-invisible at play size and reads as a plant icon, not a beautiful ore.
A thin sprig floating in a soft radial glow; too slight to read as veinlight ore or as a trap, and it does not match the cracked-vein ore look.
Spiky sea-green domes glow and catch light on the floor tops; a bright swimmer overhead competes for focus in a polyp shot.
Polyps light the tops of the tiles they sit on and the rock below; spikes and slit mouths read, MAELIS green is correct.
Volumetric swirl and glowing eye read clearly as a current with an eye; the swimmer is in frame so the riptide-carries-creatures idea reads.
Strong eye, streaking particles show flow direction, swimmer visible at left; sea-green haze fills the space without flattening the dark.

top_issues.issue: Brinewyrm silhouette is a closed ring with no head or mouth
top_issues.why: A threat must read as a threat at play size; a looped torus reads as jewellery, and the octahedron head has no eye, jaw or fangs.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep it in an open S or breaching arc and give the head a clear faceted jaw and a glowing eye so the dangerous end points at the player.

top_issues.issue: Frostbloom is too slight to read as an ore
top_issues.why: The brief wants a beautiful glowing veinlight ore with a subtle tell; a lone white sprig disappears in the gameplay frame.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build it from the veinlight tile language (cyan glow plus branching white veins) and add one small tell, such as a petal-like split or a slow pulse.

top_issues.issue: Swimmer intrudes on the polyp shot
top_issues.why: A bright cyan centipede at the top of the frame is the brightest object and pulls the eye from the polyps.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep swimmers in riptide habitats or dim them when they are away from the current.

top_issues.issue: Brinewyrm emissive is weak relative to its pool
top_issues.why: The pool, not the creature, is the light source; the wyrm is lit by the water rather than lighting it.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the wyrm a cyan core or vent glow that brightens the water around it as it moves.

protect: Riptide's volumetric swirl, streak particles and glowing faceted eye
Polyp glow landing on the tops of adjacent floor tiles
Brinewyrm's glowing cyan brine pool and pearl/violet faceted body palette
Frostbloom's cyan halo bleeding into the tile below

per_shot.note: Stretched swimming pose reads as an eel/wyrm with a trailing tail; brighter, more saturated pool glows and washes its rim.
Clear long-body silhouette and lovely brine light, but the head is still a featureless octahedron with no eye or jaw.
Starburst crystal reads at play size and looks like a valuable ore; the violet tile has little halo, so its glow barely lands on the stone.
Faceted ice star is beautiful and low-poly; the spikes hint at a bite, but it looks like its own ore type rather than veinlight with a subtle tell.
Polyps glow with a large soft green aura in the air; the floor tops catch less light than in A, but the shot is uncluttered.
Green light sinks into the rock column beneath; the tops of the neighbouring tiles stay dark, so the light lands less on the surface.
Same strong swirl and eye; the swimmer is cropped at the frame edge, so the carried-creatures idea reads less.
Eye and current read clearly and are well centred; no swimmer in frame.

top_issues.issue: Brinewyrm head has no dangerous end
top_issues.why: The body now reads as a wyrm, but the head is a blank octahedron, so the threat does not point anywhere.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a faceted jaw wedge and a glowing eye on the leading end; let the head be the brightest part.

top_issues.why: The violet tile reads as a flat panel; the glow does not spill onto the neighbouring rock the way ore and creatures should.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the starburst but sit it in a cyan bloom that washes the adjacent tiles, with violet only as the accent on the tell.

top_issues.issue: Frostbloom does not read as veinlight ore
top_issues.why: The brief calls for a trap disguised as veinlight ore; a distinct star crystal reads as a different item rather than a disguise.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Start from the veinlight branching-vein tile and let the star facets be the subtle tell.

top_issues.why: The riptide's identity is a current that carries other creatures; without a swimmer in frame it reads only as a vortex with an eye.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep at least one swimmer orbiting inside the swirl near the eye.

protect: The saturated, bright brine pool that lights its rim
Frostbloom's faceted starburst, which reads at play size
Riptide's volumetric swirl, streak particles and glowing eye
The polyps' soft sea-green aura in the dark

why: B fixes the two weakest creatures: the brinewyrm finally reads as a swimming wyrm and the frostbloom reads at play size. A keeps a slight edge on polyp light landing on the floor and on showing the riptide swimmer.
